comment: The airdress-cli revision every server build uses: the tag AND the commit it must resolve to, so a moved tag stops the build instead of changing what ships. Read by server-build.yml (release and the reproducibility check alike). v0.1.0 is the first tag of airdress-cli's collapsed history (2026-10-07); every earlier tag is gone from that repository, so an older pin cannot be fetched. On 2026-10-08 that history was rewritten to conventional commits with identical trees, so v0.1.0 now names f5eed7e; the source it builds is byte for byte the same. On 2026-10-09 the pin moved to v0.1.3: static musl Linux builds, and credentials kept by the real Secret Service rather than the keyring library's in-memory mock store that every earlier musl build used. On 2026-10-09 airdress-cli was made public as a fresh repository, its history re-created as signed bot commits with identical trees, so v0.1.3 now names d0cdbf0; the source it builds is byte for byte the same. On 2026-10-10 the pin moved to v0.1.6 (316258753c66): the chat tools say an airdress's agent devices are off instead of advising a device join it would refuse, and the server carries airdress-cli's changes since v0.1.3. On 2026-10-14 the pin moved to v0.1.7 (e9bd69694d69): login opens the browser and waits for the approval, with the device flow kept for another device; rustls 0.23.46, and serde_norway for serde_yaml. On 2026-10-22 the pin moved to v0.1.10 (4769ab106fda): sessions are named, `@name` in chat reaches only that session, the bus addresses sessions by name, and the server takes --configured-session-name for the plugin's session_name setting. The same day it moved again to v0.1.11 (da52f5c4856d): a changed root or device key is reported as its own verdict (root_changed or device_key_changed, with signature_valid) instead of 'invalid', and `airdress agent bus repin` moves the pin after a person checks the new fingerprint. On 2026-10-23 it moved to v0.1.12 (eacc5c46886f): where the operator keeps session names (its /info lists session_names) the server registers, renames and posts by them, so a restarted session gets its name back and a clash is settled by the operator; the device host keeps the names of the sessions waiting on it; and an @-mention matching no session is answered with who is here and the near name. The same day it moved again to v0.1.13 (83923c72167e): a restarted session gets its pinned name back from the device host instead of a -3 suffix, a removed agent device waits for its Welcome instead of asking to rejoin, and system notices reach a session with their words. Then to v0.1.14 (4c1e8d42c3ea): a conversation with a named session is that session's alone, and what is written to it while it is not running reaches it when it starts. On 2026-10-24 it moved to v0.1.16 (d90d32d2451a): a session reaches a named session on another airdress by name@airdress (v0.1.15), the reachable_from_contacts setting opts one in, a message from another airdress reads as signed by that airdress's device and checked by this airdress's operator instead of 'invalid', and a session started before its device host joins the bus once the host is up. On 2026-10-24 it moved to v0.1.17 (918bd8dc7e7c): every message reaches every session and only the one addressed acts; each pushed message says who sent it and what it may ask (own devices and sessions request, everyone else informs unless the owner widened them); a reply in chat is signed by the session that wrote it, so a phone shows its name only when the signature holds; and a session finds a device host started from a shell without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. On 2026-10-24 it moved to v0.1.18 (caccba210d9f): a session that finds the plugin's session name held by another session on the machine takes a random name instead of a numbered one, and is told how to choose. The same day, before 0.1.12 was tagged, it moved to v0.1.19 (d511e4e6899d): a fresh machine needs fewer steps (login makes its own profile, device join takes the account's only airdress, the server starts the device host itself, and 'no device' says how to get one).
